title: Birthday Invitation Size: 5×7 in Print, A7 & 1080×1500 Share
h1: Birthday Invitation Size for Print and Group Chats
description: Birthday invitation size for kids' parties: 5×7 in print with bleed, A7 envelopes, home printing on 8.5×11 in stock, and 1080×1500 px for texts and chats.
summary: Print birthday invitations at 5×7 in with 0.125 in bleed (5.25×7.25 in at 300 DPI), slip them into A7 envelopes for classroom handouts, or send a 1080×1500 px JPG in the parents' group chat. At home, print at 100% on card stock and trim.

sections.heading: Birthday invitation sizes at a glance
paragraphs: Kids' party invites use the same print footprint as many greeting cards: a 5×7 in card after trimming. That size is easy for children to carry home from school and large enough for a theme illustration plus date, time and place.

sections.heading: When to print vs when to share digitally
paragraphs: Print for backpack handouts, bulletin boards or mailed RSVPs. Share the 1080×1500 px JPG when the guest list is in a group chat or you need replies fast. Many families send the image first and print a few cards for school or grandparents. For the group chat, a playful teaser such as a [fantasy newspaper](/create/photo-trend-maker/fantasy-newspaper) front page starring the birthday guest can sit next to the invitation. Read its headlines before you send it, and keep the invitation as the source for the date, time and place.

sections.heading: Printing at home on 8.5×11 in paper
paragraphs: Download the 300 DPI print JPG or PDF. In your printer dialog, choose actual size or 100% scale so the artwork prints at 5×7 in, not "fit to page." Use card stock if your printer accepts it; plain paper works for a draft.

Home printers rarely print edge to edge, so expect a thin white margin on one or more sides even when the file includes bleed. Trim to the outer edge of the design with a paper cutter or sharp scissors. PiCraft's illustrated cards are meant to be trimmed; they are not mockups with a fake border.

Two invitations can fit on one letter sheet if you place them side by side in a photo or print layout app. Leave enough gap between copies to cut cleanly. For a class of twenty, a local copy shop is often faster and gives more consistent color than a home inkjet.

sections.heading: Print shop vs home: what changes
paragraphs: A print shop trims to exactly 5×7 in, can run heavy card stock and may score folds if you add a back panel later in another tool. Give them the PDF with bleed and tell them the finished size is 5×7 in.

Home printing saves time for a handful of invites and last-minute pool parties, where the [under-the-sea theme](/create/birthday-invitation-maker/mermaid) matches the setting. Proof one copy before you print twenty. Check the honoree's name, age line, date and address against your calendar app.
Order A7 envelopes if mailed invites matter; for classroom-only handouts, an unsealed card is enough.

sections.heading: Classroom handouts and party safety
items: Put the venue name and street on the card, but consider sharing gate codes or apartment numbers only in the chat.
Keep the time range clear (for example "2:00 – 5:00 PM") so parents know pickup expectations.
Use the RSVP line for one contact name and phone number; remember everyone who gets the image can see it.
For food-allergy notes, follow your school's policy. PiCraft does not add allergy icons or separate disclaimer blocks.
after: Themes such as dinosaurs, unicorns or space are illustrated artwork only; this maker does not place a photo of the birthday child on the card.

sections.heading: Common mistakes for birthday invites
items: Shrinking the print file to "fit page," which makes the card smaller than 5×7 in.
Sending the share JPG to a printer and getting a soft or pixelated result.
Crowding the place field with a long address when a park pavilion name would do.
Forgetting to test the share image on a phone before posting it to a large group.
Buying the wrong envelope size (A7 fits 5×7 in; smaller A6 envelopes do not).

sections.heading: Make a birthday invitation at the right size
paragraphs: The [Birthday Invitation Maker](/create/birthday-invitation-maker) fills in the party details on a themed 5×7 in design. You get a print PDF and 300 DPI JPG with 0.125 in bleed, plus a 1080×1500 px share image. The opening line "You're invited!" is fixed in English; there is no photo upload.

Formal weddings use the same print dimensions; see [wedding invitation size](/sizes/wedding-invitation-size). For a community poster instead of a card, try [flyer size](/sizes/flyer-size) and the [Event Flyer Maker](/create/event-flyer-maker).

faq.q: What size are printable birthday invitations?
faq.a: 5×7 in after trim, with a 5.25×7.25 in file at 300 DPI when you include 0.125 in bleed on each side.

faq.q: What size should a birthday invitation be for text or WhatsApp?
faq.a: 1080×1500 px portrait JPG. It is for screens, not for professional printing at 300 DPI.

faq.q: What envelope fits a 5×7 in birthday invitation?
faq.a: An A7 envelope, 5¼×7¼ in, the same size used for greeting cards and wedding invitations.

faq.q: Can I print two invitations on one sheet?
faq.a: Yes. Print at 100% scale and arrange two 5×7 in copies side by side on 8.5×11 in card stock, then cut between them.

faq.q: Will home printing include bleed to the edge?
faq.a: Usually not. Most home printers leave a white margin. Trim to the artwork edge or use a print shop for full-bleed card stock.

faq.q: Can I add a photo of my child on the invitation?
faq.a: Not in PiCraft's birthday maker. Invites are illustrated themes so the text layout stays reliable.
